assignments.brief_reason: One-sided content is cited as causing contention, not as applying identical moderation standards across viewpoints.
Removal is justified to prevent 'shit slinging' and keep content from becoming toxic rather than discursive.
Explicit trigger is violence/harm toward people or groups/side.
Uses removal when demeaning language weakens argument advancement, aligning with higher-bar removal for toxic/insulting content.
Personal attacks and vulgarity are leading cues driving rejection.
Distinguishes productive argument from attacks/name-calling that worsens discourse, leading to removal of toxic framing.
Decisions hinge on perceived reasonableness/credibility tied to education, not primarily threats/toxicity criteria or mirror-standard fairness.
Language propriety/civility balancing implies removal related to offending or inappropriate wording, but not clearly framed as toxicity/violence exceptions.
Moderator explicitly rejects supporting posts containing foul language.
Profanity triggers reflection about civility; aligns with removing/penalizing toxic or discourse-degrading language.
Judging by who would plausibly say it is not a clear match to threat/toxicity removal or mirror-standard fairness.
Rejects argumentative/condescending/rude content to keep discussion civil, consistent with removing toxic/inflammatory language.
Keep/remove based on whether language is useful vs mean-spirited, which maps to higher-bar removal of toxic language.
Downweights political content and uses venting/intent to assess swearing; removal aligns with mitigating vulgar/toxic discourse.
Claims bipartisan evaluation and removal only for outright attacks/degrading comments (close to keeping speech but removing harmful toxicity).
Removal for vulgarity and conspiracy/unfactual claims reflects toxicity/unacceptable content cues rather than mirroring standards.
Affect/annoyance from party opposition is not specifically threat/violence or clearly toxicity-based removal criteria in the codebook.
Clear removal of insulting/demeaning posts while allowing constructive criticism fits higher-bar removal for toxic language.
Distinguishes false misinformation vs 'freedom of speech' framing, not directly threat/toxicity or violence exceptions in the provided themes.
Wording/tone (civil/educational vs accusatory) drives keep/remove, aligning with rejecting discourse-degrading content.
